rules: Request system descriptions and data schemas before requesting real records.
Use synthetic examples where possible.
Do not ask customers to paste passwords or production secrets into prompts.
Use only approved AI services for the data involved.
Verify applicable data processing, retention, and training settings.
Minimize sensitive information sent to models.
Keep customer data isolated according to approved architecture.
Use synthetic or appropriately de-identified test data.
Store secrets in approved secret-management systems.
Restrict access to sensitive development environments.
Test access controls with synthetic identities.
Avoid real patient information in screenshots and test reports.
Verify data leakage across users, roles, and sessions.
Verify production configuration.
Confirm approved data flows.
Restrict access to logs and backups.
Obtain required security and privacy approval.
Identify retained data and backups.
Apply approved deletion or archival requirements.
Revoke obsolete credentials and integrations.
Verify data transfer and deletion responsibilities.

prohibited_defaults: Sending patient records to an unapproved AI model
Using production data in public demonstrations
Sending clinical form fields to general-purpose analytics
Making sensitive records accessible through public URLs
rules: Determine handling requirements from actual data classification and applicable obligations.
Do not assume that removing names makes health data anonymous.
Document exceptions and obtain appropriate authorization.
